title: Gold Attribute Mapping
description: Defines Silver→Gold attribute mappings for one domain's gold table in the medallion architecture. One file per domain (e.g. product, order). Replaces the *-gold-attribute-mapping-template.xlsx workbook: each 'column' entry is a config-only change that engineering turns into master schema + lineage + mapping SQL.

$schema.description: Path to this schema file, for editor validation.

domain.description: Domain this mapping file covers, e.g. 'product'. One mapping file per domain.

table.description: Fully qualified gold table this mapping targets, e.g. 'gold_product.product'.

drivingTable.description: The Silver source table that IS the entity's spine: the gold table gets one row per (filtered) row of this table. Sources equal to it need no join; every other source attaches to it via sourceRef.join (directly or through a chain). Named here once so tooling never has to infer the entity's driving table.

drivingSilverTable.description: The driving table's fully qualified Silver name with the environment templated (e.g. uif_echo_{env}_silver_tep.xxpso_inv_stock_atp_stg). Required by the new-entity scaffolder (UIFPE-260): the compiler must not guess which Silver database a table lives in, and it runs where no catalog is reachable. The wizard fills it from the silver catalog the author picked the table from.

silverTables.description: Bare source-table name -> fully qualified Silver name with the environment templated (e.g. QP_LIST_HEADERS_B: uif_echo_{env}_silver_tep.qp_list_headers_b). Required by the new-entity scaffolder for every LOOKUP table a column or nested field reads (UIFPE-262) — same rationale as drivingSilverTable: the compiler must not guess databases and runs where no catalog is reachable. The wizard fills it from the silver catalog.

drivingFilter.description: Row filter over the driving table — a SQL boolean predicate defining which source rows belong to the entity (e.g. PPID IS NOT NULL). The scaffolder writes it into BOTH the generated SQL's WHERE and the manifest's sot_filter, keeping the platform invariant (SQL domain == reconcile's source-of-truth domain) true by construction. Only the new-entity scaffolder consumes it; the add-column compiler refuses intakes that carry it, because retrofitting a domain filter into shipped SQL is a hand-reviewed change.

rowGroups.description: Named row groups for Proliferate fan-out — user-maintained rule sets, defined ONCE per mapping and referenced by branch scopes (scope.group). Every column fanning out by the same business grouping uses literally the same predicate; renaming or extending a group is a one-place change.

entityKey.description: The gold table's PRIMARY KEY, ordered: each entry maps a gold key column to the driving-table column it comes from (product: inventoryItemId ← INVENTORY_ITEM_ID, organizationId ← ORGANIZATION_ID). This is the grain every attribute attaches to — the wizard prefills joins from it, grain derives from it (a join carrying the full key keeps the entity grain; a subset fans out across the remaining key), and a new entity's scaffold reads it for the runtime key_mapping/primary_key_cols. Optional during migration; every new mapping declares it. BOUNDARY: every key column comes from the DRIVING table — lookups contribute attributes, never key columns (product's organizationId comes from the org-replicated items table, not the org dimension). A grain no single Silver table carries (a grain-defining JOIN spine) is deliberately not expressible here — that is an architecture decision touching the CDC key_mapping invariants (ADR-0003), to be designed when the first such entity arrives.

transforms.description: Named transformation rules — user-maintained, defined ONCE per mapping and referenced by column transforms ({"rule": "pearsonImageUrl"}). Same single-source-of-truth pattern as rowGroups: every attribute using a rule compiles literally the same SQL; extending a rule is a one-place change.

registry.description: This mapping file's own Apicurio registry coordinate (../schema/guidelines.md §1, apicurio-governance.md) — declared in the artifact itself, not only known to whoever runs the registration command. Optional: a mapping file's registration can stay deferred (e.g. metadata.lifecycle: draft on the paired master.json) while still declaring the coordinate it will register under.

group.description: Apicurio artifact group — the owning domain, matching the top-level 'domain' field.

artifact.description: Apicurio artifact id. Per ADR-0023 this is '{domain}.{entity}.{type}' with type 'mapping' for this artifact kind, e.g. 'product.marketing-copy.mapping'. The former '<entity>-gold-attribute-mapping' form is superseded.

compatibility.description: Compatibility rule Apicurio enforces on this artifact. The normative Pearson standard requires BACKWARD_TRANSITIVE on data schema artifacts (FULL_TRANSITIVE on the event envelope); the transitive modes were absent from this enum until ADR-0023, so a conformant value could not be declared at all. Defaults to BACKWARD if omitted, which is weaker than the standard requires — declare it explicitly.

tier.description: Criticality tier, required at registration by the normative standard's D21: T1 critical, T2 standard, T3 observational. Drives retention, DLQ alerting, parallel-run window and contract-test depth, so it is the data owner's call. It is registry metadata and changeable without a schema version bump.

note.description: Optional free-text context, e.g. why registration itself is still deferred even though the coordinate is declared.

batch.description: Metadata about the submission that introduced/changed these columns.

requestedBy.description: Name or email of the requester.

backfillMode.description: Whether existing products' new values are pushed to consumers on backfill (emit) or just appear quietly (silent).

newChannel.description: Name of a brand-new consumer channel needed for these attributes (e.g. 'datafeed'), or null if none.

dataType.description: number = exact decimal (money, quantities). float = approximate (measurements, rates).

channels.description: Which consumer feeds carry this attribute. All attributes are always stored in the gold table regardless of channels.

goldColumnName.description: camelCase gold column / field name. May use one level of dot notation for namespaced columns (e.g. `fulfillmentOrgDetails.sellingRestrictionCode`).

joinGrain.description: DEPRECATED (UIFPE-104): attachment is now explicit — every non-driving source (EAV included) declares sourceRef.join with its ON key pairs, and proliferation is expressed solely by branch scope + rowGroups. Accepted for backward compatibility while old files migrate; new entries must not carry it.

transformDef.description: A structured transformation compiled DETERMINISTICALLY around the source expression {x} — never prose. steps = a pipeline (applied in order); cases = a guarded CASE WHEN evaluated in order with an else of keep|null. Both may be combined: cases run first, steps wrap the result. sqlExpr is the gated escape hatch for genuinely custom logic: a SQL fragment containing {x}, flagged for engineering review by CI.

sqlExpr.description: Escape hatch: SQL fragment with {x} as the source expression. CI flags every use for engineering review.

transformRef.description: A column's transform: null = straight copy; {rule} references a named transforms entry; an inline transformDef defines one in place. Prose strings are DEPRECATED (UIFPE-105) — accepted while old files migrate; new entries must be structured.

table.description: Source Oracle/PDH table. Not restricted to a fixed list: attributes sourced from any other Oracle table are welcome and will register a Bronze→Silver pipeline for that table first.

join.description: How this source table attaches to the entity — REQUIRED for every source that is not the driving table, EAV tables included (their entity-key join is stated explicitly, e.g. ON INVENTORY_ITEM_ID [+ ORGANIZATION_ID]). Structured — never prose — so the compiler renders the JOIN deterministically and the UI can display it. leftTable must be the driving table or another already-joined source (chains compose: A -> B -> C).

type.description: left keeps entity rows without a match; inner drops them. Default left.

discriminatorRef.description: The Table.Column whose value decides which branch applies.

rowGroupDef.description: A named row group: either a positive predicate over an entity-grain column, or the COMPLEMENT of another named group ('everything not in ukOrgs') — the complement follows its base definition automatically, so the pair can never drift apart.

table.description: Entity-grain table the column lives on (e.g. the org dimension MTL_PARAMETERS); null if it is a gold column.

description.description: What this group means to the business, incl. the current membership if helpful.

complementOf.description: Name of a PREDICATE row group this group is the complement of — every row NOT in that group. Must not reference another complement.

branchScope.description: Proliferate grain only: WHICH entity rows receive this branch's value. Either a REFERENCE to a named rowGroups entry ({"group": "ukOrgs"} — preferred, single source of truth) or an inline predicate. The complement branch uses op=else = every row no sibling branch's scope claimed. Two branches may share one discriminator condition and differ only in scope.

group.description: Name of a rowGroups entry — the scope IS that group; inline fields are then omitted.

table.description: Entity-grain table the scope column lives on (e.g. the org dimension MTL_PARAMETERS); null if it is a gold column.

op.description: startsWith renders LIKE 'value%'. else = every row no sibling branch's scope claimed.

label.description: Human name for an inline row group, e.g. 'non-UK orgs'.

condition.description: The discriminator value this branch applies for ('10002', optionally labeled '10002 (Digital)'), or 'ELSE'. Row-group qualifiers do NOT belong here — use scope.

fallback.description: What to do when this branch's source value is empty: return NULL, or fall back to the ELSE branch's value.

sortKey.description: At least one field in the array must have sortKey: true; multi-key sorts compose in field order (UIFPE-262). Not enforceable in pure JSON Schema — validated separately.

source.description: null = declared with no Silver source yet; the column is rendered NULL until a source registers.

conditionalColumn.description: For attributes whose source depends on a discriminator (e.g. digital vs physical items read different ATTR_GROUPs).

transform.description: Column-level transform applied AFTER the branch pick — it wraps the value the winning branch produced (e.g. URL normalization applied to whichever catalog's cover image won). A branch's own transform applies before the pick, to that branch's expression only.

nestedColumn.description: For 1-to-many attributes (e.g. BOM components, contributors) — a product has many.

joinKey.description: How rows attach to the product, e.g. 'BILL_SEQUENCE_ID -> item'.

filter.description: WHERE fragment shared by all fields in this array, if any.

fields.description: One entry per field inside each array element. At least one must have sortKey: true — multi-key sorts are the norm (UIFPE-262), and a pick's partitionBy must be covered by the sort keys.

pick.description: Declarative ranked pick (UIFPE-262, new-entity scaffolds only): before the array is assembled, keep ONE source row per partition — row_number() over partitionBy, ordered by the orderBy expressions, rn = 1. This is how 'the ACTIVE price if one exists, else the latest end-dated' is said without hand-writing SQL. NOTE: the whole final SELECT reads pick winners, so SCALAR aggregates also see only the kept rows. orderBy expressions may reference field names (resolved to their projections) and driving columns; aggregates and windows refuse. The scaffolder requires every partitionBy field to also be a sort key of the array, so element order stays total and the canonical hash stays stable (the A8 lesson).

partitionBy.description: Field names (from this column's fields) that define one array entry — the pick keeps one source row per distinct combination, per entity.

expr.description: A Spark SQL ordering expression over the source columns (e.g. CASE WHEN END_DATE IS NULL OR END_DATE >= current_timestamp THEN 0 ELSE 1 END). Review-gated like sqlExpr transforms.

derivation.description: ADR-0008 (Accepted 2026-08-26): the query is the contract. A column whose value takes several steps to work out carries the author's actual SELECT plus a small declared contract; the compiler wraps the query as a CTE under the column's name and LEFT-joins it on the declared entity columns — the wrap is the ONLY transformation, so the reviewed SQL is the running SQL and there is nothing to drift. NOT a fourth kind: an optional block on a column of any kind (kind = the value's shape; derivation = how the value is reached). Governance is the validation battery (derivation_chain.py, run at submit and in CI): one read-only Spark SELECT, registered source aliases only, stable results (no run-varying functions; collects state their ordering), contract columns present in the projection — plus the live one-row-per-entity test run the wizard offers, and PR review before deploy (ADR-0006).

sql.description: The author's own query — ONE read-only SELECT, Spark SQL dialect, reading only this entity's REGISTERED runtime aliases (items_ext, items_all, related, ... — never raw Silver table names). Must return at most one row per entity; lists and structs are built INSIDE the query (array_sort(collect_list(...)), named_struct(...)) so the output row is always the final value.

keyedBy.description: Which output column(s) identify the entity each row belongs to — the join contract for the compiler's LEFT join back to the driving table. entityColumn is the DRIVING-TABLE column joined against (an entity key column, or a value column like SEGMENT1 for reverse-keyed shapes); _ID entity columns are CAST AS BIGINT at the join (the A3 rule).

valueColumn.description: Which output column carries the value. Defaults to the goldColumnName.

reads.description: Which registered aliases and columns the query reads — COMPUTED by the validator from the parsed query and re-checked in CI, never typed by hand. Self-healing lineage: a stale entry fails the gate.
